description:
One fact per function on the World with two bits. `allocates`: the lowered body contains a heap-allocating primitive, or calls a function whose fact says allocates. `fails`: the body reaches `fz_panic` (the only `never` extern) directly or through a callee. Both bits only turn on, so the formula is monotone and a call cycle converges through the ordinary dependency scheduler: no SCC solver, no private cone. The fact reads LoweredBody(f), StaticCallees(f) and the callees' effects facts, and moves only when one of those moves.

Externs. `extern "C"`: allocates = false, fails = false; it has no process, so it cannot touch the fz heap, and its own memory is not ours. `extern "fz"` is opaque Rust, so the bit is declared on the declaration line. Finding: `fz_value_cmp_ref` is `extern "fz"` because atom order reads the atom table through the process, not because it allocates; deriving the bit from the ABI would refuse every `<` in a guard except number against number. Proposed spelling, open for decision: `extern "fz" pure defp fz_value_cmp_ref(any, any) :: integer`, where `pure` means allocates = false; `:: never` already means fails.

Allocation is judged after lowering. A construction of static shape whose value does not escape the activation rides in lanes and is not an allocation; anything of unbounded size (list construction, binary concatenation, map update) is. That line is where the BEAM's guard BIF set sits (hd, tl, element, byte_size, map_get, binary_part and arithmetic; no ++, no <>, no map construction), reproduced by construction rather than by a list. Hence the two prerequisites: the arithmetic pair in lanes and the bitstring reader in lanes, or the fact classifies `+/2` and every binary pattern as allocating.

Consumers: guard compilation refuses an `allocates` callee and activates a `fails` callee in guard mode; the matcher contract is this fact enforced on everything the matcher runs.

What goes away once the consumers land: the syntactic whitelist in `guard_expr_from_ast`, `resolve_guard_callee*`, `collect_guard_calls_in_*`, `GuardCallCycle`, the "not dispatch-pure" diagnostics.

Proof: a unit test stating the fact for `+/2`, `compare/2`, `</2`, `send/2`, a list literal, and a mutually recursive pair; a telemetry pin that an edit to an unrelated body moves no effects fact and an edit to a leaf callee moves exactly its transitive callers' facts.
title: One effects fact per function on the World: allocates and fails
